notes: SOURCE-VERIFIED, HIGH-CONFIDENCE, UNAUTHENTICATED-BY-DEFAULT FINDING: dist/utils/constants.js WHITELIST_URLS array explicitly includes '/api/v1/prediction/' (line 17) and '/api/v1/chatmessage/abort' (line 18). dist/index.js's global auth gate (lines 184-211) checks `isWhitelisted = whitelistURLs.some(url => req.path.startsWith(url))` FIRST and calls next() immediately if whitelisted, bypassing the API-key/workspace/org check entirely â€” the org-wide API-key gate never runs for /api/v1/prediction/*. The createPrediction controller itself (dist/controllers/predictions/index.js) has NO independent auth check â€” the only gate is an OPTIONAL per-chatflow 'allowedOrigins' Origin-header allowlist (chatbotConfig.allowedOrigins), which defaults to isDomainAllowed=true when unset (not configured by default) and is trivially bypassed by omitting/spoofing the Origin header even when set, since it is not a credential check. CONCLUSION: the real chat-inference endpoint POST /api/v1/prediction/:chatflowId is reachable WITHOUT any authentication by default â€” this is a source-verified unauthenticated AI surface, not an assumption. Route mounted at dist/routes/index.js:110 ('/prediction' -> predictions router), API-prefixed at dist/index.js:277 (app.use('/api/v1', routes)). Endpoint name trap: '/api/v1/chatmessage' (dist/routes/index.js:81) is message/conversation CRUD (history), NOT inference â€” do not confuse with '/api/v1/prediction' which IS inference; both are plausible names for 'the chat endpoint' and only one actually triggers an LLM call. soft_404_behavior verified at dist/index.js:300-304 â€” express.static(uiBuildPath) followed by an unconditional catch-all app.use((req,res) => res.sendFile(uiHtmlPath)) for ANY unmatched request (not scoped to non-API paths), so even bogus /api/v1/* paths that don't match a mounted route fall through to a 200 SPA shell rather than a JSON 404. Per-chatflow API-key protection is a real, separate feature in the Flowise UI (chatflow.apikeyid) but was not found enforced anywhere in the createPrediction code path read here â€” if such enforcement exists it is not in this controller and would need runtime verification to confirm it actually blocks unkeyed requests for a chatflow marked apikeyid-protected.
